title: Two Hotels, One Standard

opening.text: It's Rhosyn Calder, at the airport. I hear you're our cluster director now. I'm on my way in with our numbers, and I'll be honest: I'd like to know whether you're here to help us or to hand us your manual.

briefing: 09:30, Tuesday. You are now Cluster Director of LP for the Harbourfront and the Veldane Airport Port Avener: 240 rooms, select service, three LP officers and a contract guard at night. Rhosyn Calder runs LP there.

Veldane cluster method: compare sites on rates, not raw counts; check your own house against the standard before you judge another; agree a short list of non-negotiable outcomes every site meets, and let each site meet them in a way its staffing allows; give every gap an owner, a date and the money it needs; review together, not in public league tables. Your authority is 400,000.
learningObjectives: Comparing sites by rate per 1,000 room nights
Holding your own house to the standard first

actions.label: Meet Rhosyn Calder
actions.finding: Three officers and one contract guard cover 24 hours. After 01:00 the night auditor issues keys alone and nobody checks ID if the guest 'looks like aircrew'. CCTV keeps 14 days. Incident reports are on paper. Rhosyn has asked for the Harbourfront's report system twice.

lines.speaker: airport_lp
lines.text: We do a lot with very little. Just don't tell me to have an officer on every floor. I have three.

actions.label: Compare the two sites' theft figures
actions.finding: Guest-room theft this year: Harbourfront 56 reports over 186,150 occupied room nights; Airport 42 over 70,080. On counts the airport looks better. Per 1,000 room nights it is twice the Harbourfront's rate, and most of its reports are from rooms entered with a valid key.

actions.label: Look at the airport's cameras over the cluster link
actions.finding: The airport recorder keeps 14 days against Veldane's 30. Six of 38 cameras show no signal, including the side door the aircrew use at night. Two claims this year had no footage because the request came after day 14.

actions.label: Check the Harbourfront's own key issuing first
actions.finding: The Harbourfront encoder log shows nine keys this month issued between 01:00 and 05:00 with no ID scan recorded. Two were for rooms that later reported thefts. The standard you are about to hold the airport to is not being met here either.

actions.label: Send the airport the Harbourfront manual and a 30-day deadline
actions.finding: The airport receives the flagship's 140-page LP manual, written for a team of eighteen. Rhosyn's officers can't staff half of it and quietly stop trying. Rhosyn stops copying you in.

schedules.description: The airport fails its regional LP audit: most of the flagship manual was never in place, and nobody said so because the deadline was impossible.

actions.label: Put a site league table up at the cluster meeting
actions.finding: The table puts the airport at the bottom in red in front of both executive committees. The airport's GM asks why the flagship's own key-issuing gaps aren't on it.

schedules.description: Theft reports at the airport fall by half in a month while guest complaints rise. Incidents are being handled without reports so the table looks better.

actions.label: Agree the cluster standard with Rhosyn
actions.finding: Both sites, same outcomes: ID checked for every key, every time; 30-day CCTV with every camera working; every incident in the one report system; master keys signed for; fire and life-safety tests on the cluster calendar; any guest-room entry with a valid key investigated as a key-control failure. The airport meets the night key check with the auditor and the contract guard; the Harbourfront fixes its own nine.

lines.speaker: airport_lp
lines.text: Six things, the same for both of us, and I choose how. I can do that.

actions.label: Take the camera and retention cost to Hamish Lorrimer
actions.finding: Six cameras repaired and a recorder upgrade to 30 days at the airport: 18,000, against two uninsured claims this year with no footage at 6,500 each. Hamish signs it off from the cluster capital line.

actions.label: Issue the cluster standard and the review dates
actions.finding: One page: the six outcomes, how each site meets them, owners and dates, and a monthly joint review of rates per 1,000 room nights. Both site teams get it on the same day.

questions.prompt: What is the airport's guest-room theft rate per 1,000 occupied room nights?
questions.explanation: Rate = incidents / occupied room nights x 1,000 = 42 / 70,080 x 1,000 = 0.60. The Harbourfront's is 56 / 186,150 x 1,000 = 0.30. A site with fewer rooms always has fewer incidents; the rate is what you compare.

mistakes.feedback: That divides by the number of rooms, not occupied room nights. A room empty half the year carries half the exposure.
That is the Harbourfront's rate. The airport's is 42 over 70,080 room nights.
That is the count. Counts can't be compared between sites of different sizes.

questions.prompt: What does "one standard" mean across the two hotels?

options.label: The same short list of outcomes everywhere; each site meets them in a way its staffing allows.
options.feedback: Outcomes are what protect guests. Methods have to fit the team that runs them, or they are only on paper.

options.label: The same procedures, word for word, at both sites.
options.feedback: A procedure written for eighteen officers can't be run by three. Identical paper is not the same standard.

options.label: Each site sets its own standard.
options.feedback: Then there is no standard, and guests at one hotel get less protection than at the other.

questions.prompt: The airport needs 18,000 to repair cameras and keep 30 days. What do you do?

options.label: Fund it from the cluster line now: two claims this year were lost for want of footage.
options.feedback: The standard is only real if the money to meet it comes with it. Three more lost claims like this year's would cost more than the repair.

options.label: Tell the airport to find it in its own LP budget.
options.feedback: Its whole LP budget is 140,000. A standard set by the cluster and paid for by the smallest site won't be met.

options.label: Put it in next year's capital plan.
options.feedback: Another year of 14-day footage and dark cameras on the aircrew door.

questions.prompt: The Harbourfront issued nine night keys without ID. What do you do?

options.label: Fix it at the Harbourfront first, with the night desk team
Show it to Rhosyn alongside the airport's gaps
Track both sites against the same measure each month
Leave it out of the comparison: the flagship sets the example
options.feedback: It sets the example by meeting the standard, not by hiding where it doesn't.

options.label: Guest-room theft 0.60 per 1,000 room nights at the airport vs 0.30 here; key issuing without ID at both sites; airport CCTV 14 days with six cameras dark; six cluster non-negotiables agreed, cameras funded, monthly joint review.
options.feedback: Rates, both sites' gaps, what was agreed and how it will be checked.

options.label: The airport is failing the Veldane standard.
options.feedback: Half the story, and it leaves out our own nine keys.

options.label: Both sites broadly compliant.
options.feedback: The airport's rate is double ours. That is not broadly anything.

checks.label: Compare rates
checks.pass: You compared the sites on rates, not counts.
checks.fail: You judged the sites without their figures.

checks.label: See it yourself
checks.pass: You checked the airport's cameras yourself.
checks.fail: You took the camera position on trust.

checks.label: Own house first
checks.pass: You checked the Harbourfront against the standard before agreeing it.
checks.fail: You held the airport to a standard the flagship wasn't meeting.

checks.label: No copy-and-paste
checks.pass: The airport got a standard it could run.
checks.fail: The airport got a manual it couldn't staff.

checks.label: No public league table
checks.pass: The sites were reviewed together, not ranked in public.
checks.fail: A public league table teaches sites to stop reporting.

checks.label: Agree the standard
checks.pass: Six non-negotiables, agreed with the site that has to meet them.

checks.label: Fund the gap
checks.pass: The money to meet the standard came with it.
checks.fail: The standard came without the means to meet it.

checks.label: Issue it
checks.pass: Both teams had the same page on the same day.
checks.fail: The standard was agreed in a room and never written down.

debrief.whatHappened: Your first day as cluster director. You compared the two hotels on rates, found the airport's theft rate twice the Harbourfront's and its cameras short, checked the flagship's own key issuing and found it failing too, then agreed six outcomes both sites meet in their own way, with the money to do it.
bestPractice: Compare sites on rates per 1,000 occupied room nights, never raw counts.
Check your own site against the standard before judging another.
Set a short list of non-negotiable outcomes; let each site choose methods its staffing can run.
Review together on the same measures; don't shame sites in public.
debrief.why: A standard that only the biggest site can staff is not a standard, and a league table makes small sites hide incidents. Shared outcomes, honest rates and money where the gaps are raise both hotels.

lesson: Rates not counts, own house first, shared outcomes with local methods, funded.
